canonical.title: Balanced Binary Tree
canonical.sourceFilePath: 11. Binary Trees/2. Medium Problems/02. Balanced Binary Tree.cpp

narrative.title: The Load-Balance Rigging Audit
narrative.scenario: A stage-rigging contractor hangs lighting trusses from a binary tree of support arms. Insurance rules say the structure is certified only if, at every junction, the two hanging chains differ in length by at most one unit — otherwise torque builds up dangerously. The auditor needs a single pass that certifies or condemns the whole rig before the show is booked.
narrative.inputFormat: The root of a binary tree given as a level-order array where null marks a missing child. An empty array is a valid (empty) tree.
narrative.outputFormat: Return true if the tree is height-balanced at every node, false otherwise.

testCases.explanation: Every junction's two chains differ by at most one unit.
At the root, the left chain runs 3 deep but the right chain only 1 — a gap of 2.

hintLevels: Level 1: Checking heights naively re-measures subtrees repeatedly — the audit wants one trip, not one trip per node.
Level 2: Fold two answers into each recursion frame: the subtree's height and whether it is already balanced.
Level 3: A subtree is balanced iff both children are balanced and their heights differ by at most 1; bubble any failure straight to the top.
